title: World War II (1939–1945)
summary: The causes of World War II, Hitler's expansion and appeasement, the main events in Europe and the Pacific, South Africa's role and the end of the war.

items: **The Treaty of Versailles (1919)**: Germans resented losing land, paying reparations and accepting war guilt.
**The Great Depression (from 1929)**: mass unemployment and poverty made people turn to extreme leaders who promised solutions.
**The rise of dictators**: Mussolini (Italy, 1922), Hitler (Germany, 1933) and military leaders in Japan wanted to expand their countries.
**Failure of the League of Nations**: it had no army and could not stop Japan invading Manchuria (1931) or Italy invading Ethiopia (1935).
**Appeasement**: Britain and France gave in to Hitler's demands to avoid war.

rows: German troops re-occupied the Rhineland, breaking the Treaty of Versailles
**Munich Agreement**: Britain (Chamberlain) and France allowed Germany to take the Sudetenland from Czechoslovakia; Chamberlain claimed 'peace for our time'
Germany occupied the rest of Czechoslovakia
**Nazi-Soviet Pact**: Germany and the USSR agreed not to fight each other and secretly to divide Poland
Germany invaded **Poland**. Britain and France declared war on 3 September

notes.text: The policy of giving in to the demands of an aggressive country in the hope of avoiding war.

notes.title: Why appeasement failed
notes.problem: Explain why Britain's policy of appeasement failed.
steps: Britain and France let Hitler take the Sudetenland at Munich in 1938, hoping for peace.
Hitler took the rest of Czechoslovakia in March 1939.
He invaded Poland on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France declared war.
notes.answer: Each concession encouraged Hitler to demand more.

rows: Britain and its empire (including South Africa), France, the USSR (from 1941), the USA (from 1941), China

items: **Blitzkrieg** ('lightning war'): fast attacks with tanks and aircraft conquered Poland, Denmark, Norway, the Netherlands, Belgium and France by June 1940.
**Battle of Britain (1940)**: the RAF defeated the German air force, preventing an invasion of Britain.
**Operation Barbarossa (June 1941)**: Germany invaded the USSR. The German defeat at **Stalingrad** (1942–1943) was a turning point.
**Pearl Harbor (7 December 1941)**: Japan attacked the US naval base in Hawaii, bringing the USA into the war.
**D-Day (6 June 1944)**: Allied forces landed in Normandy, France, to free Western Europe.
**Germany surrendered on 8 May 1945** (VE Day) after Hitler's suicide.

notes.text: The war in the Pacific ends

Japan kept fighting. On **6 August 1945** the USA dropped an **atomic bomb** on **Hiroshima** and on **9 August** on **Nagasaki**, killing more than 200 000 people. Japan surrendered on 15 August (formally on 2 September 1945).
South Africa and World War II

items: Parliament voted narrowly to join the war on Britain's side; **Jan Smuts** became Prime Minister. Some Afrikaner nationalists opposed the war, and the Ossewabrandwag carried out sabotage.
About 330 000 South Africans volunteered. They fought in East Africa (Ethiopia), North Africa (Tobruk and El Alamein) and Italy.

Black and coloured men served in the **Native Military Corps** and Cape Corps but were mostly not allowed to carry arms. **Job Maseko**, a prisoner of war, sank a German ship at Tobruk using an improvised explosive and received the Military Medal.
Industry grew rapidly during the war, drawing many black workers to the cities.

notes.label: Results
notes.text: About **70 to 85 million people** died, the majority of them civilians. The **United Nations** was formed in 1945, Europe was divided between the USA and the USSR, and colonies began demanding independence.

notes.title: A divided country at war
notes.problem: Why was South Africa's entry into the war controversial?
steps: In September 1939 Parliament voted narrowly, 80 to 67, to join Britain.
Many Afrikaner nationalists opposed fighting on Britain's side.
Jan Smuts replaced Hertzog as prime minister.
notes.answer: White politics was deeply divided over supporting Britain.
